 Judgment
In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 13.08.2013 in M.V.C.No.62/2011 passed by II Additional Sessions and Special Judge, Bengaluru ('the Tribunal' for short).

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, the husband of 1st petitioner, father of petitioner No.2 and son of respondents No.4 and 5 by name Gurumurthy, the deceased, met with an accident on Kolar-Bengaluru main road at Hosakote town in front of Ambedkar Colony, while travelling as a pillion rider in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/ED-3060, hit by a tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53/A-2139 from behind killing him at the spot.

The petitioners being the dependents S Shashikala vs Praveen Kumar on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7398986/
2 have moved the Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by respondents No.1 to 3.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, passed the impugned judgment awarding compensation of Rs.21,47,824/- with 6%
interest.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking NC: 2023:KHC:33623 enhancement, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Chandrashekhar.

R, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. B.
Pradeep, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was a graduate, he is a Trained Technical Staff working as a Plumber, employed permanently at Atreya Engineers and Consultants in Bengaluru, drawing a salary of more than Rs.16,000/- per month.

In spite of his employment and income proof is produced before the Tribunal, it has disbelieved the income and Rs.14,430/- has been assessed by the Tribunal, compensation under conventional heads is also not properly awarded and sought for enhancement.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has rightly considered the avocation of the deceased, his income only after considering the materials, has correctly assessed the salary and thereby assessed the loss of dependency, compensation under conventional heads is adequate, there is no need for enhancement and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The material on record did point out that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter, respondents No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased.
Ex.P18 to 27 are the certificates and marks cards pertain to the deceased for SSLC, PUC, JVC and BA.
The deceased is said to be the trained person working as a Plumber.
Ex.P12/pay slip and NC: 2023:KHC:33623 Ex.P13/bank statement of the deceased point out that the deceased was employed at Atreya Engineers and Consultants at Bengaluru as a Plumber.
The material on record also points out that the deceased was born on 04.04.1979 and he was aged 32 years on the date of accident in the year 2011.
The claim of the petitioners is two-fold.
One is improper assessment of income and the other is inadequate award of compensation under conventional heads.
Ex. P12
/ pay slip points out that the deceased was drawing a gross salary of Rs.15,730/- and his net salary is Rs.15,530/- after effecting statutory deduction of professional tax of Rs.200/-.

To show that the deceased was receiving the regular salary as a permanent employee, Ex.P13/bank statement points out that in the month of April 2011,
the salary paid to the deceased was Rs.16,054/-, where in the month of May, he died in the accident.
I have perused the impugned judgment.
There is no ground to accept the reason assigned by the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:33623 in not relying upon Ex.P12.
Hence, the income of the deceased has to be assessed at Rs.15,530/-.

sentences.text: There are 4 dependents of the deceased.
Hence, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Since the deceased is aged less than 40 years, future prospects has to be added at 50% as he is a person with permanent job, drawing salary.

9.1. By applying the above principles, taking the income of the deceased at Rs.15,530/-, loss of dependency shall be calculated as follows:
Rs.15,530/- + Rs.7,765/- (50%) = Rs.23,295/- - (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:33623 Rs.5,824/- (1/4th) = Rs.17,471/- x 12 x 16 (multiplier) =
Rs.33,54,432/-.
Towards loss of consortium to wife, loss of love and affection to petitioner No.2 and respondents No.4 and 5, a sum of Rs.20,000/- each is assessed.
Towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.10,000/- each is assessed.

By summing up, total compensation comes to Rs.34,54,432/- as against Rs.21,47,824/-
assessed by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.13,06,608/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioners and respondents No.4 and 5 are entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.

Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.

NC: 2023:KHC:33623 iii) Petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.13,06,608/- with interest of 6% p.a.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
v) Regarding apportionment is concerned, the award of the Tribunal is kept intact.
vi) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
